title: Born in Talwandi
told: the Janamsakhi tradition of Guru Nanak’s birth

hook.say: before the story, a question. do you know the story of the day you were born?
options: then you know how families tell it. listen.
then let’s start with someone else’s. listen.

steps.line: Spring, 1469, in Punjab. A mud-brick village called Talwandi sat among the wheat fields, southwest of Lahore.
steps.label: from the Janamsakhi tradition

steps.line: Its landlord was a Muslim, Rai Bular. His village accountant was a Hindu, Mehta Kalu. And Kalu’s wife, Mata Tripta, was about to have a baby.

steps.q: The janamsakhis, the old life-stories of Guru Nanak, surround his birth with signs. What do they say filled the room?
steps.why: Light. The tellers wanted you to see it.

steps.line: The old stories say that when the baby came, the little room filled with light. The midwife, a Muslim woman named Daultan, said she’d never seen a child like him.
steps.label: a traditional story

steps.line: His big sister, Nanaki, was about five. The baby was named Nanak.

steps.q: A Muslim landlord, a Hindu father, a Muslim midwife. Why might Sikhs love these details?
o: They show the family was well off
They echo his words: no Hindu, no Muslim
They show Punjab had no conflict then
steps.why: Years later he’d say, “There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim.” His story began among Hindu and Muslim neighbors.

steps.line: Talwandi is now called Nankana Sahib, Nanak’s town, in Pakistan. A gurdwara stands where tradition says he was born, and Sikh pilgrims still travel there.
steps.label: today

steps.line: Sikhs celebrate his birth at the autumn full moon, with lights and all-night singing, though the oldest accounts say spring. Scholars still debate it.
steps.label: today

steps.q: His big sister Nanaki was five when he was born. What does Sikh tradition remember her as?
o: The one who taught him to read
The first to see who he was
The one who arranged his marriage
steps.why: Many Sikhs call Bebe Nanaki the first to recognize her brother’s light. Later he lived with her in Sultanpur.

steps.q: The baby’s name, Nanak, echoes his sister’s, Nanaki. Hers came from where she was born. Where?
steps.why: Nanke is Punjabi for your mother’s family home, where Nanaki was born, many say. Then her baby brother got a name to match.

say: sikhs tell the birth stories with joy. what can be said plainly is where, and roughly when: a small village, an ordinary family.
and that’s part of the point. no palace, no crowd. guru nanak taught that the one light shines in everyone. it fits that his own story began somewhere small, among muslim and hindu neighbors.

steps.q: The oldest accounts put his birth in spring, yet Sikhs celebrate at Kartik’s full moon. Where does the autumn date come from?
o: One janamsakhi, the Bala, gives it
The day he first set out to teach
steps.why: The Bala janamsakhi gives the Kartik full moon; the Puratan gives spring, in Vaisakh. Love for the Bala telling carried the day.

today.say: today, ask someone who was there about one small detail of your beginning: the weather, the room, who came first. every story starts somewhere small. yours too.
options: then write it down when you hear it.
then say the name of the place, quietly. that’s enough.

tomorrow.title: The sister who saw first.
tomorrow.line: everyone worried about the dreamy boy. one person didn’t.
